29630-the-curse-of-education.title: Curse of Education
29630-the-curse-of-education.creator: Harold E. Gorst
29630-the-curse-of-education.description: A book by Harold E. Gorst. Year by year this fact is becoming more emphasized. During the past century almost every civilized country applied itself feverishly to the invention of a national plan of education, with the result that the majority of mankind are compelled to swallow a uniform prescription of knowledge made up for them by the State. Now there is a great outcry that England is being left behind in this educational race. Other nations have got more exact systems.

74802-the-sweet-miracle.creator: Unknown
74802-the-sweet-miracle.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. IN those days Jesus had not yet departed from Galilee and the fair luminous margins of the Lake of Tiberias; but the news of his miracles had already penetrated as far as Enganim, a rich city of strong battlements set among vineyards and olive-groves in the Country of Issachar.

arxiv-2206-08763.title: Solving small-scale clustering problems in approximate lightcone mocks 2022 Solving small-scale clustering problems in approximate lightcone mocks – References
arxiv-2206-08763.creator: Alex Smith, Shaun Cole, Cameron Grove, Peder Norberg, Pauline Zarrouk
arxiv-2206-08763.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Alex Smith, Shaun Cole, Cameron Grove, Peder Norberg, Pauline Zarrouk. Realistic lightcone mocks are important in the clustering analyses of large galaxy surveys. For simulations where only the snapshots are available, it is common to create approximate lightcones by joining together the snapshots in spherical shells. We assess the two-point clustering measurements of central galaxies in approximate lightcones built from the Millennium-XXL simulation, which are constructed using different numbers of snapshots.

arxiv-2302-09516.title: A Bibliography of Multiple Sclerosis Lesions Detection Methods using Brain MRIs
arxiv-2302-09516.creator: Atif Shah 1,2, Maged S. Al-Shaibani 2, Moataz Ahmad 2, Reem Bunyan 3
arxiv-2302-09516.description: Abstract Introduction: Multiple Sclerosis (MS) is a chronic disease that affects millions of people across the globe. MS can critically affect different organs of the central nervous system such as the eyes, the spinal cord, and the brain. Background: To help physicians in diagnosing MS lesions, computer-aided methods are widely used.

arxiv-2309-15338.title: Counterintuitive patterns on angles and distances between lattice points in high dimensional hypercubes
arxiv-2309-15338.creator: Jack Anderson, Cristian Cobeli, Alexandru Zaharescu
arxiv-2309-15338.description: Abstract . Let 𝒮 \mathcal{S} be a finite set of integer points in ℝ d \mathbb{R}^{d} , which we assume has many symmetries, and let P ∈ ℝ d P\in\mathbb{R}^{d} be a fixed point. We calculate the distances from P P to the points in 𝒮 \mathcal{S} and compare the results.

arxiv-2401-10132.title: Trapped Vortex Dynamics Implemented in Composite Bessel Beams
arxiv-2401-10132.creator: Andrew A. Voitiv, Mark E. Siemens, Mark T. Lusk
arxiv-2401-10132.description: Abstract The divergence-free nature of Bessel beams can be harnessed to effectively trap optical vortices in free space laser propagation. We show how to generate arbitrary vortex configurations in Bessel traps to investigate few-body vortex interactions within a dynamically-evolving fluid of light, which is a formal analog to a non-interacting Bose gas.

arxiv-2402-16555.title: Boundary-induced transitions in Möbius quenches of holographic BCFT
arxiv-2402-16555.creator: Alice Bernamonti, Federico Galli, Dongsheng Ge
arxiv-2402-16555.description: Abstract Boundary effects play an interesting role in finite-size physical systems. In this work, we study the boundary-induced properties of 1+1-dimensional critical systems driven by inhomogeneous Möbius-like quenches. We focus on the entanglement entropy in BCFTs with a large central charge and a sparse spectrum of low-dimensional operators.

arxiv-2503-16692.title: Limits of trust in medical AI
arxiv-2503-16692.creator: Joshua Hatherley
arxiv-2503-16692.description: Abstract Artificial intelligence (AI) is expected to revolutionise the practice of medicine. Recent advancements in the field of deep learning have demonstrated success in variety of clinical tasks: detecting diabetic retinopathy from images, predicting hospital readmissions, aiding in the discovery of new drugs, etc.

arxiv-2504-09848.title: A Survey of Large Language Model-Powered Spatial Intelligence Across Scales: Advances in Embodied Agents, Smart Cities, and Earth Science
arxiv-2504-09848.creator: Jie Feng, Jinwei Zeng, Qingyue Long, Hongyi Chen, Jie Zhao, † Yanxin Xi, Zhilun ZhouYuan Yuan, § Shengyuan Wang, Qingbin Zeng, Songwei Li, Yunke Zhang,Yuming Lin, Tong Li, Jingtao Ding, Chen Gao, Fengli Xu, Yong Li
arxiv-2504-09848.description: Abstract Over the past year, the development of large language models (LLMs) has brought spatial intelligence into focus, with much attention on vision-based embodied intelligence. However, spatial intelligence spans a broader range of disciplines and scales, from navigation and urban planning to remote sensing and earth science. What are the differences and connections between spatial intelligence across these fields?

pmc-10670670.title: Potential Use of PLA-Based Films Loaded with Antioxidant Agents from Spent Coffee Grounds for Preservation of Refrigerated Foods
pmc-10670670.creator: Margherita Pettinato, Maria Bolla, Roberta Campardelli, Giuseppe Firpo, Patrizia Perego
pmc-10670670.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). The aim of this work concerned the production of an active food packaging suitable for refrigerated foods. Polylactic-acid-based films were produced by optimizing the solvent casting technique and testing different loadings of extracts obtained from spent coffee grounds. Indeed, an extract obtained by high-pressure and -temperature extraction (HPTE) and a further purified extract by liquid–liquid extraction (LLE) were separately used as active agents, and the effects on packaging features and active compounds migration were analyzed.

pmc-10671422.title: Tff3 Deficiency Differentially Affects the Morphology of Male and Female Intestines in a Long-Term High-Fat-Diet-Fed Mouse Model
pmc-10671422.creator: Kate Šešelja, Iva Bazina, Milka Vrecl, Jessica Farger, Martin Schicht, Friedrich Paulsen, Mirela Baus Lončar, Tatjana Pirman
pmc-10671422.description: Trefoil factor family protein 3 (Tff3) protects the gastrointestinal mucosa and has a complex mode of action in different tissues. Here, we aimed to determine the effect of Tff3 deficiency on intestinal tissues in a long-term high-fat-diet (HFD)-fed model. A novel congenic strain without additional metabolically relevant mutations (Tff3-/-/C57Bl6NCrl strain, male and female) was used.

pmc-10703976.title: Linguistic Illusions Guide Eye Movement: Evidence From Doubling
pmc-10703976.creator: Qatherine Andan, Peter Bex, Iris Berent
pmc-10703976.description: Across languages, certain phonological patterns are preferred to others (e.g., blog > lbog). But whether such preferences arise from abstract linguistic constraints or sensorimotor pressures is controversial. We address this debate by examining the constraints on doubling (e.g., slaflaf, generally, XX). Doubling demonstrably elicits conflicting responses (aversion or preference), depending on the linguistic level of analysis (phonology vs. morphology).

pmc-11399141.title: Juvenile responses to immune challenges are not carried through to subsequent life stages in an insect
pmc-11399141.creator: Farley W S Silva, Daniel L Viol, Simon L Elliot
pmc-11399141.description: Environmental variability can significantly impact individual survival and reproduction. Meanwhile, high population densities can lead to resource scarcity and increased exposure to parasites and pathogens. Studies with insects can offer valuable insights into eco-immunology, allowing us to explore the connections between these variables.

pmc-11494099.title: Non-averaged single-molecule tertiary structures reveal RNA self-folding through individual-particle cryo-electron tomography
pmc-11494099.creator: Jianfang Liu, Ewan K S McRae, Meng Zhang, Cody Geary, Ebbe Sloth Andersen, Gang Ren
pmc-11494099.description: Large-scale and continuous conformational changes in the RNA self-folding process present significant challenges for structural studies, often requiring trade-offs between resolution and observational scope. Here, we utilize individual-particle cryo-electron tomography (IPET) to examine the post-transcriptional self-folding process of designed RNA origami 6-helix bundle with a clasp helix (6HBC).

pmc-11672505.title: Cyclic Peptide MV6, an Aminoglycoside Efficacy Enhancer Against Acinetobacter baumannii
pmc-11672505.creator: Natalia Roson-Calero, Jimmy Lucas, María A Gomis-Font, Roger de Pedro-Jové, Antonio Oliver, Clara Ballesté-Delpierre, Jordi Vila, Marisa Di Pietro, Piyush Baindara
pmc-11672505.description: Background/Objectives: Acinetobacter baumannii is a globally emerging pathogen with widespread antimicrobial resistance driven by multiple mechanisms, such as altered expression of efflux pumps like AdeABC, placing it as a priority for research. Driven by the lack of new treatments, alternative approaches are being explored to combat its infections, among which efficacy-enhancing adjuvants can be found.

pmc-12397467.title: CD44 overexpression as a mediator of drug resistance in oral cancer: a meta-analysis unveiling molecular underpinnings and therapeutic implications
pmc-12397467.creator: Shushu Miao, Caiqiong Wang, Anqi Zheng
pmc-12397467.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). BackgroundTherapeutic resistance in oral cancer, with cancer stem cells (CSCs) playing a pivotal role, remains a major clinical challenge. CD44, a key CSC marker, has been implicated in multidrug resistance mechanisms through drug efflux, DNA repair, and anti-apoptotic pathways.

pmc-13239487.title: Endodontic Diagnosis and Nonsurgical Management of a Maxillary Second Molar With Parastyle: Report of a Case With a 24‐Month Follow‐Up
pmc-13239487.creator: Konstantinos Ioannidis, Eirini Sakellaridi, Myron Bitsakis, Nikolaos Economides
pmc-13239487.description: Parastyle is a rare dental morphological trait characterised by an accessory cusp or tubercle, often found unilaterally on the buccal surface of the mesiobuccal cusp, mainly in the second and third maxillary molars. Its size may range from a small enamel pit to an independent, well‐developed cusp.

pmc-13662249.title: The Sacro-Femoral-Pubic Angle May Estimate Pelvic Tilt in Patients with Severe Developmental Dysplasia of the Hip and Leg Length Discrepancy Undergoing Total Hip Arthroplasty
pmc-13662249.creator: Özgür Avci, Alpaslan Öztürk, Yavuz Akalın, Nazan Çevik, Oğuz Çetin, Furkan Yeşilbursalı
pmc-13662249.description: BackgroundSpinopelvic movement disorders are associated with instability after total hip arthroplasty (THA). In patients with Crowe type 3–4 developmental dysplasia of the hip (DDH) and leg length discrepancy (LLD), sagittal radiographs may not allow accurate assessment of spinopelvic motion. This study aimed to evaluate the sacro-femoral-pubic (SFP) angle, a coronal plane parameter, as a predictor of calculated pelvic tilt (PT).
